episode_in_one_sentence: Coordinated agents tackled formal mathematics while individual builders found smaller, immediately usable ways to make autonomous tools part of ordinary work and life.

listener_notes.note: The solitary-Claude framing contradicted the collaborative-agent description, while reportedly weakened a direct OpenAI statement.
The original horizon-problem sentence carried too many steps in one breath.
The original voice-agent pitch repeated the YouTube desk's opportunity.
Repeated comparisons with other agents delayed the personal-errand idea.
A solo developer's command center for more than thirty sessions was the strongest grounded builder story.
The two proof efforts and their Lean artifacts give the episode its memorable spine.

after_evidence.hook: The 89-word opening names Anthropic and OpenAI's mathematical proof efforts in its first breaths and asks how far a coordinated crew can go.
after_evidence.audience_fit: The desks favor robotaxis, a livestream build, a solo developer's dashboard, portable skills, visual and voice tools, storefront advertising, and personal errands.
after_evidence.inspiration: Each desk turns a concrete development into a small build, creative experiment, or personal use case; the close offers three playful tries.
after_evidence.caution_budget: No caution-language warning appears outside Research. The sole reality check holds three plain items, though its delivery is slightly shorter than the suggested 45 seconds.
after_evidence.specificity: Waymo's fifteenth market, thirty concurrent sessions, more than a thousand skills, five-cent voice pricing, and the two mathematical efforts anchor the desks.
after_evidence.non_redundancy: YouTube owns conversational speech and horizon framing; Launches owns purchasable voice access; Social owns personal errands. Only generic agent vocabulary recurs.
after_evidence.clarity_for_ear: Zero sentences exceed thirty words, with an 11.7-word average reported by lint.
after_evidence.momentum: The episode moves from mobility and speech to a live build, a solo command center, portable skills, consumer launches, personal agents, and research.
after_evidence.voice_distinctness: Marcus is enthusiastic about videos and voice, Priya is clipped and playful, Sam narrates a scrappy maker, Maya explains portability, and Aaron slows for mathematics.
after_evidence.flow_and_handoffs: All seven desks hand back; quick pivots, pre-sting pickups, and the Grok Bot callback vary the transitions.
after_evidence.accuracy: The opening says largely autonomously and dozens of Claude agents; the Navier-Stokes result is attributed directly to OpenAI. Fermat is no longer called a Millennium Prize problem.
after_evidence.tts_readiness: Version numbers, amounts, and the command-line interface are spoken naturally; lint reports zero symbol and long-sentence issues.
after_evidence.close: Jordan offers a voice guide, a shared skill, and iterative image edits, followed by three opportunity-oriented watch items.

warnings_left_by_design.reason: The remaining cross-desk terms are generic connective words and the central subject, agents; each desk owns a distinct use rather than repeating the same advice.

summary_for_producer: The draft had an inaccurate solitary-Claude hook, unnecessary hedging on OpenAI's directly stated Navier-Stokes result, and twelve overlong sentences. The edit preserves its opportunity-first energy while giving each desk a distinct use case and each story an actionable spark. All cautions sit in Research's reality check, the close has three enjoyable tries and three opportunity watches, and lint finishes with zero errors and no caution-language warning. Next week, keep an eye on generic agent vocabulary even when the underlying stories differ.
